hmmt-feb-2008-calc-02.title: Tangency condition
hmmt-feb-2008-calc-02.body:
Let the tangent point be $(t,t^3+t+16)$. The slope from the origin is $\frac{t^3+t+16}{t}$ and the slope of the curve is $3t^2+1$. Equating: $t^3+t+16=3t^3+t$, so $t^3=8$, $t=2$ and the slope is $3\cdot4+1=13$.

**Answer: 13**

hmmt-feb-2008-calc-03.title: Integrate by parts
hmmt-feb-2008-calc-03.body:
With $u=\ln x$, $dv=x\,dx$: $\int_1^y x\ln x\,dx=\frac12y^2\ln y-\frac14y^2+\frac14$. Setting this equal to $\frac14$ gives $y^2\left(\frac12\ln y-\frac14\right)=0$, hence $\ln y=\frac12$ and $y=\sqrt e$ (the only solution, since $y>1$).

**Answer: $\sqrt e$**

hmmt-feb-2008-calc-04.title: Force a zero denominator, then L'Hopital
hmmt-feb-2008-calc-04.body:
The numerator tends to $0$, so the denominator must too: $1+a+b=0$. By L'Hopital the limit equals $\lim\frac{-2\ln(2-x)/(2-x)}{2x+a}$, whose numerator again tends to $0$, so $2+a=0$. Thus $a=-2$, $b=1$.

Check: $x^2-2x+1=(x-1)^2$ and $\ln(2-x)=-(x-1)+O((x-1)^2)$, so the ratio tends to $1$.

**Answer: $(a,b)=(-2,1)$**

hmmt-feb-2008-calc-05.title: Simplify f
hmmt-feb-2008-calc-05.body:
With $s=\sin^2 u$, $c=\cos^2u$: $s^3+c^3=(s+c)^3-3sc(s+c)=1-3\sin^2u\cos^2u=1-\frac34\sin^22u=\frac58+\frac38\cos4u$. With $u=x/4$: $f(x)=\frac58+\frac38\cos x$.

Since $2008=4\cdot502$, $f^{(2008)}(x)=\frac38\cos x$, so $f^{(2008)}(0)=\frac38$.

**Answer: $\frac38$**

hmmt-feb-2008-calc-06.title: Squeeze
hmmt-feb-2008-calc-06.body:
Let $S_n$ be the sum. The terms $k=0$ and $k=n$ give $2$, so $S_n\ge2$. For $n\ge3$ the terms $k=1$ and $k=n-1$ give $\frac2n$, and each of the remaining $n-3$ terms is at most $\binom n2^{-1}$, so $S_n\le2+\frac2n+(n-3)\binom n2^{-1}\to2$. Hence the limit is $2$.

**Answer: 2**

hmmt-feb-2008-calc-07.title: Expand with t = 1/x
hmmt-feb-2008-calc-07.body:
Write $\sqrt[3]{x\pm1}=x^{1/3}\sqrt[3]{1\pm t}$ with $t=\frac1x$. Using $\sqrt[3]{1\pm t}=1\pm\frac t3-\frac{t^2}9+o(t^2)$, the bracket equals $x^{1/3}\left(-\frac29t^2+o(t^2)\right)\sim-\frac29x^{-5/3}$. So $x^p\cdot x^{-5/3}$ has a finite non-zero limit iff $p=\frac53$.

**Answer: $\frac53$**

hmmt-feb-2008-calc-08.title: Spot the derivative
hmmt-feb-2008-calc-08.body:
Divide numerator and denominator by $e^x$: the integrand is $\frac{2e^{2x}+e^x-e^{-x}}{e^{2x}+e^x-1+e^{-x}}$, and the numerator is exactly the derivative of the denominator. So $T=\left[\ln(e^{2x}+e^x-1+e^{-x})\right]_0^{\ln2}=\ln\left(4+2-1+\frac12\right)-\ln2=\ln\frac{11}4$.

Therefore $e^T=\frac{11}4$.

**Answer: $\frac{11}4$**

hmmt-feb-2008-calc-09.title: Take logarithms, recognise a Riemann sum
hmmt-feb-2008-calc-09.body:
The logarithm is $-\frac12\left(1+\frac1n\right)\ln n+\frac1{n^2}\sum_{k=1}^nk\ln k$. Since $\sum_{k=1}^n k=\frac{n(n+1)}2$, we have $\frac1{n^2}\sum k\ln n=\frac12\left(1+\frac1n\right)\ln n$, which cancels the first term. What remains is $\frac1{n^2}\sum k\ln\frac kn=\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^n\frac kn\ln\frac kn\to\int_0^1x\ln x\,dx=-\frac14$.

So the limit is $e^{-1/4}$.

**Answer: $e^{-1/4}$**

hmmt-feb-2008-calc-10.title: Series expansion
hmmt-feb-2008-calc-10.body:
$\ln(1-x)=-\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{x^n}n$, and $\int_0^1x^n\ln x\,dx=-\frac1{(n+1)^2}$ (by parts). So the integral is $\sum_{n\ge1}\frac1{n(n+1)^2}$.

Partial fractions: $\frac1{n(n+1)^2}=\frac1n-\frac1{n+1}-\frac1{(n+1)^2}$. The first two telescope to $1$, and $\sum_{n\ge1}\frac1{(n+1)^2}=\frac{\pi^2}6-1$. Total: $1-\left(\frac{\pi^2}6-1\right)=2-\frac{\pi^2}6$.

**Answer: $2-\frac{\pi^2}6$**
